subject: ventures/wedding-photographer-profit-calculator
professional: a working wedding photographer who runs a small studio, with a CPA who prepares Schedule C returns for creative sole proprietors; first check: does profit per hour worked reconcile to a real package P&L and does tax appear anywhere

evidence.correctness: Ran analyze() on packages 'a,4200,8,350,2' and 'b,900,2,40,1' with overheadMonthly=1000 and defaults, then recomputed independently in a separate Python script (not the author's code). Slot hours 32.5 and 11.5 matched; profit/hour 104.98 and 63.55 matched; price floor 2357.88 and 739.32 matched; weekly revenue 2325.00, contribution 2025.25, own weekly 1775.25 matched. Raise break-even at +10% = extra/(C+extra) = 10.02% matched by closed form. Lead and associate model weekly (1542.75 and 150) follow from stated formulas; checked by reading, not independently priced. Not run against a real photographer's books (the README says so).
evidence.completeness: Claimed features checked: packages parser with header skip and warnings (works, tested), travel/client/editing hours per job (works), headline vs worked rate (works), price for target (works), own vs lead vs associate comparison (works), raise break-even and retention table (works), CSV export (reportCsv works), local usage counters with opt-out (usage.mjs, 3 tests). index.html wires the same calc.mjs. I did not load the page in a browser; page.test.mjs checks its static content only. No stubs or TODOs found in calc.mjs.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/wedding-photographer-profit-calculator && node --test '*.test.mjs': 30 pass, 0 fail. Seeded three separate mutations in calc.mjs, each reverted with git checkout (tree clean after): editHours halved (29 pass, 1 fail, caught), net = price*(1+fee) (1 fail, caught), lead fee divisor 100 to 200 (1 fail, caught). Tests are example-based with hand numbers; no property or randomized tests, and no test cross-checks floorPrice by plugging it back to profitPerHour == target.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (152 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, usage.mjs header, index.html wiring. Pure functions, frozen defaults, input validation returns {error} not throws, a warning when the mix needs more hours than are bookable. Defects: num() maps blank to default silently and a non-numeric option string also becomes NaN then an error (fine) but parsePackages silently counts-only skipped lines; overheadPerHour spreads overhead over all bookable hours rather than hours actually used, so low utilization understates overhead per worked hour (profitPerHour is flattering); associate weekly mixes hours that exclude overhead; magic 1e-9 tolerance fine. Display helpers money/pct untested for NaN.
evidence.claims: README and page claims checked: no data uploaded (page.test asserts the statement; the code has no network call in calc.mjs), disclaimer 'No warranty ... not legal, tax, or financial advice' present in index.html line 132 and README, not-modelled list present at index.html line 111 (tax, retainers, seasonality, albums), 'tested on hand-calculated examples' is true. VENTURE.yaml stage is prototype, consistent. Not independently verified: the 'about 3x as many hours of editing as coverage' framing in VENTURE.yaml is an assumption the user can change (editRatio default 2.5), and is presented as such.
evidence.fitness: Walked a photographer through the sample six packages: they get worked-hour profit, price floor and model comparison in one screen, which answers 'what do I earn per hour worked'. Gaps they hit within an hour: no income or self-employment tax, so the 'profit' per hour is pre-tax and a $50 target is not take-home; no fixed per-job time per package (travel, client time and edit ratio are global, not per package, so an engagement session and a full wedding share the same 3 client hours); no seasonality or capacity cap that rejects an infeasible mix beyond a warning; no way to model second shooter wages beyond a flat cost per job. Useful but a planning sketch, not a pricing sign-off.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard photographer pricing practice (cost of doing business, then hourly rate = (salary + overhead + profit) / billable hours, as taught by e.g. PPA and Schedule C practice). The tool matches the per-hour-worked idea and uses a target hourly, but a senior practitioner would depart on: per-package editing/client hours rather than global ones, a salary-plus-tax-based target derived from required annual income and realistic billable share (35 h x 48 wk assumes 100% of bookable hours are fillable), CoGS vs overhead split for taxes, and usage-based overhead absorption. The limits are disclosed, but they are the main drivers of a real price.

defects.what: Overhead per hour is allocated across all bookable hours (35 x 48) not hours actually used, so profit per hour worked is overstated when utilization is low (sample mix at 55% utilization).
Travel, client time and editing ratio are global inputs applied to every package; an engagement session and a full-day wedding get the same 3 client hours and 1.5 travel hours.
No income or self-employment tax; the hourly target is pre-tax. Disclosed as not modelled but it is the number a photographer prices against.
Associate model gives no pay for editing/delivery handoff and subtracts only gear and a share of overhead; no mileage or travel pay.
Page not exercised in a browser by the tests; page.test.mjs only reads static HTML.

verdict: The arithmetic is right and the tests are real: six outputs matched an independent Python recomputation, and three seeded mutations were each caught by the 30-test suite. It does what its README says, and its disclaimers are honest and specific. It stops short of senior-practitioner level on method: overhead is spread over bookable rather than used hours, per-job time inputs are global instead of per package, and nothing accounts for tax, so profit per hour worked is a flattering pre-tax figure. Meets the computed bar (correctness, claims, verification all 3) but the median of seven is 3 with fitness and domain at 2; the page itself was not loaded in a browser.
